scope: Temporal duplicate acceptance test for Cosmos DROID composites
summary: The first exact-frame-hash audit falsely accepted the rejected 8-to-16 FPS dataset because H.264 reconstruction perturbed repeated frames; the replacement decoded-pixel near-duplicate audit correctly rejected it with a 50% median duplicate rate.
evidence: temporal-duplicate-audit-v1.json reported zero exact duplicates and accepted=true on the known paired-frame dataset.
Direct decoded-frame inspection showed alternating MAD values near 0.01-0.17 and ordinary-motion values commonly above 1.0 on the same clips.
temporal-near-duplicate-audit-v2.json uses decoded 0-255 pixel MAD <= 0.25 and reports median 0.5, P90 0.5104167, minimum 0.4895833, maximum 0.5520833, with accepted=false.
lessons: Lossy video coding invalidates exact decoded-hash equality as a duplicate-frame detector.
Acceptance tests must be calibrated against a known negative fixture before they gate training data.
limitations: The MAD threshold detects near-identical decoded frames but does not measure motion semantics or optical-flow accuracy.
next_actions: Run the same frozen MAD gate on the new native-16-FPS composite and require median <= 0.15 and P90 <= 0.30 before embedding.
